not calling
You almost call someone.

i had the number open because i was trying to remember the postcode. that was the excuse. walked past the station twice and on the second time a man asked if i was lost. said a bit so he started giving directions and now i had to go that way. her flat was the other way. could've called from somewhere i hadnt meant to be. could've said i left a bag. there wasn't a bag. there was but it was hers.
fringe
A friend changes something small.

leah had cut all her hair off and i said it looked nice too quickly so she didn't believe me. it did look nice. she kept touching the back of her neck and i wanted to do that too, not her neck, mine, to show i understood how it would feel. sometimes when we meet now it feels like a performance of us meeting three years ago. the same jokes in the same places. she asked about work and i said same old even though i'd been fired on thursday. i nearly told her then but the waiter came and she started explaining about the haircut, how she went in for a trim and then just said go on. i was listening, i was, but mostly i was looking at the prices and wondering if she'd notice me only having chips
Wait after the last service has gone.
it says due. it said due twenty minutes ago. there's just me and a woman holding a cake level with both hands. i hope she isnt going somewhere sad. i want to ask what flavour but that would be weird.
sofa bed
Stay with an old friend.

the sofa folded out into most of the room. i had to put my suitcase in the shower, which meant remembering to take it out again in the morning, which i didnt. max was very nice about the wet suitcase and that made it worse. we'd lived together for two years once and now he was saying things like help yourself to anything and explaining which mug i could use. i think i wanted him to be rude. to say move your stuff, idiot. his girlfriend came home while i was drying socks with her hairdryer and stood there for a second then said oh you're here. she didn't mean anything by it probably. i said sorry about the electricity. who says that.
wrong building
Hear a familiar sound in an unfamiliar place.

i followed the singing up a flight because it sounded like our old school song. not the words, the horrible tune they made us do every monday. there was a door open and maybe thirty people standing very still while a woman in gym clothes counted down from eight. i thought aerobics but there was no music. then they all shouted the same word and slapped their faces. i should've left. i stood there with a delivery bag from a place i didnt even work at anymore and watched them start again. one man saw me and mouthed don't. don't what. the lift doors opened behind me and i stepped into them without turning round and pressed the button for the ground floor about ten times.
free evening
A cancelled plan brings mixed feelings.

got ready and then she cancelled. fine, i wanted to stay home, except now i was in the jeans that hurt sitting down. went to the supermarket in them. bought olives like a person having a nice evening. i dont even like olives. ate the bread standing up then went to bed. not much of a story really.
wrong screws
Repair something that keeps breaking.

The hinge had come away because someone used the screws supplied with it. Those are for putting the thing in the packet, I swear, not for actual wood. I drilled out the holes and pushed dowel into them with glue. You have to leave that overnight. My brother said he needed the door back on tonight. I said then he should have phoned yesterday. This is how most of our conversations go now. He brought a chair into the hall and sat watching while I looked for the old tin of longer screws. His knee made a cracking noise when he sat. I was going to ask about it but he started telling me which drill bit to use, and I went back out to the van.
page seven
A manual is missing one important step.

The diagram shows the assembly rotating clockwise. There's a steel bar through the middle preventing that. Next diagram the bar has vanished. No reference number. No arrow. I took the spring housing off to look underneath, which you're specifically not supposed to do. The spring moved against my thumb. Not unwound, moved. I put the lid back and held it with my elbow. Needed the phone but it was across the bench. The spring pushed again. I don't know enough about springs to finish this, it might not be possible. The missing bar annoyed me though.
M6
Lose a very small part.

The washer went into the gravel. I found three bottle tops, a bent nail and a tiny plastic horse. No washer. Used two smaller ones nested together, which is wrong, but it held. Now I have to remember to tell him.
borrowed
Borrow something you cannot return.

Dad etched his initials on everything, even screwdrivers you got free with paint. Forty of those, no torque wrench. Mum wants the lot out by Friday. Under the empty cases I found the sander he'd said he'd never bought. Plugged it in and it jumped out of my hand. Switch taped down. Pulled the plug. Nothing in this box is ready to use.
Temporary means until it fails
A temporary repair lasts too long.

There's a length of washing line holding the exhaust up under the van. It's not actually the exhaust, it's the heat shield, but saying exhaust makes people stop asking for lifts. I put it there in May. Last week the garage told me they'd have to charge an hour to get the knots off. I said cut them. They said there were wires tied in as well. That's odd because I didn't tie any wires in. I got under it in the car park with a torch. There was my blue line and somebody else's red cable, looped right over the fuel tank. Both ends went through a hole in the floor behind the driver's seat. I hadn't drilled that hole. The torch battery went and I lay there thinking about the man I'd bought it from.
medium wave
An old device works again.

I replaced the capacitors and it came on. Hiss first, then a woman reading numbers. Nine numbers, then my old street, the one knocked down for the bypass. I wrote it all on a receipt. There was a football result printed on the back and I remembered watching that match at Dad's. Couldn't remember driving home. I took the back off the radio again. The capacitor I'd just fitted had swollen up. I was sure I'd put it the right way round. Now I wasn't.
Hold this
Let someone else do a task.

I told her to hold the torch on the bolt. She held it on my face. I said the bolt again, louder, and she went quiet. The torch settled where it was supposed to be. I couldn't get the spanner onto it because my hand was shaking. She asked if she should try. I wanted to say no but I'd already said no about the shopping and the stairs and it was getting ridiculous. I passed it over handle first.
wrong end WRONG END
Someone boards a moving train.

I got a hand on the rail and jumped and the rail came OFF. Like completely off in my hand. Train carrying on without me, me lying on the platform with a piece of train. Excellent. Joss was hanging out the door shoutign something about the bag. I still had the bag. The bag had started ticking. I ran alongside the next carriage and threw it through an open window which in retrospect was not a great plan because a woman threw it straight back. It hit my shoulder and burst. Oranges everywhere. Not the bomb bag. The other bag. Joss was still shouting but now I could hear him saying STOP THE TRAIN. How? He was on it! I was the person running along outside it with an orange down my shirt and a metal bar, oh. Metal bar. I jammed it between the platform and the wheel and immediately realised that was possibly the worst idea I had ever had because the end whipped round and
Roof number four
A chase reaches a dead end.

Three roofs fine, fourth is glass. Eli lands and keeps going DOWN. Swimming pool underneath, lucky, except the pool's draining through a hole and taking him with it. I throw the rope. It's tied to my belt. Didn't think about that. He catches it and my knees hit the edge. Guards arrive behind me, stop shooting, just watch. One says oh shit quietly. I I can't get any grip. Eli keeps shouting about a room under the pool and I'm shouting stop MOVING but he
inspection
Lose something at the worst time.

Ticket was in my mouth because both hands were full. Swallowed it. Don't ask how, I COUGHED. Inspector looking at me like this happens every day. It does not happen every day. Train stopping somewhere that isn't on the map.
No hands
An exchange does not go as planned.

We were supposed to shake hands and the chip would pass between our palms. Simple. Except he'd lost both his arms since the briefing photo was taken. He kept saying nice to meet you and I kept looking at his sleeves. In the end I dropped the chip into his drink. BAD. It fizzed, he looked down, every light in the ballroom went out. The orchestra kept playing for about four seconds, brave of them. Then the floor started tilting. I grabbed his jacket and he said wrong man. I said yes obviously and he said no I mean wrong man to save, and something huge unfolded from his empty sleeves and went through the ceiling. I still had hold of the jacket. I really should have let go before
Under the stands
Run towards something instead of away.

Everyone ran for the exits so I went under the seats. Thought there'd be a way out. Hotdog man still turning sausages in the dark. Sir there's a FIRE. He points behind me. Water coming down the steps. Not fire then. I help him onto the counter. He won't leave the cash box. Says it's got his teeth in. I laugh and lose my grip on him, which is horrible, and then the whole counter moves and we're both going over.
Map says bridge
A plan depends on bad information.

The bridge wasn't missing. It was vertical. Whole thing sticking out of the river like somebody had kicked it. So yes technically it was still THERE, thanks Mara, very helpful distinction while people are shooting at us. We went down the bank on our backsides and got into a drain big enough to crawl through. I went first. About ten metres in my torch found a pair of boots coming the other way. Boots with feet in, yes. The feet backed up. I shouted keep going and crawled faster, then heard Mara behind me go very very quiet. There were boots behind her as well. We were in a pipe with no branches and two sets of people who'd apparently had the same clever idea. I still had one grenade but not much enthusiasm for using it.
practice run
A small success after a bad start.

Missed the jump, hit the water, lost a shoe. Did get the flag though. Coach said that didn't count because I'd touched the bottom. I said the bottom was full of eels and therefore should count double. He was writing something on his clipboard. Probably my name under never again. The flag was bleeding on my hand. I'd grabbed the wrong thing. It unfolded a little and looked at me and I decided to keep that part to myself.
six months of lentils
A space crew receives the wrong supplies.

The crate was marked medical so of course we left it sealed while we ate the insulation off the biscuit packs. Turns out it contained lentils. Forty kilos of lentils and a little bag of cinnamon someone had tucked into a corner. I wanted to hug the bag. Pavel wanted to know how we were supposed to cook them without using our drinking water. I said soak them in the coolant. He thought I meant it. That's how bad things had got, we were seriously considering the coolant. We put one mugful in the pressure chamber with steam from the laundry vent. They came out hard in the middle and tasting of everyone's socks. We ate them anyway. Then the chamber door wouldn't shut and the pressure light came on and I was trying to scrape a lentil out of the seal with my fingernail when Pavel said
free surface
A meal is interrupted by a technical fault.

Gravity went while I was swallowing. I don't know why that surprised me more than the hot soup lifting out of the bowl but it did. There was this horrible second where I thought swallowing needed gravity. It doesn't. The soup hit the ceiling in a long orange ribbon and began coming back down, not down, towards the fan. Everyone started grabbing towels. Except the new medic who grabbed a spoon and was trying to catch mouthfuls. We had explained the fans on day one. You cannot let liquid into that fan. I threw my towel at his head and he shouted at me, then the fan coughed and we had soup mist in every room including the room with the exposed sample trays. Six months of fungus research now contained carrot. Dr Iven was standing in the doorway with her glasses all orange and I honestly couldn't read her expression.
preheat
An appliance refuses to cooperate.

The oven says open door. Door is open. It says close door. Door is closed. Now it says remove occupant. I have never seen that message before. I can see right through the oven and there is nothing in it.
Mum's flatbread
Try to recreate a taste from memory.

Flour first. What kind? No idea. Mum slapped dough between her hands and I tried that, got it on the console and in my hair. Cooked it anyway. Gan ate three and asked if it was a religious dish. I said it's bread. He said bread is religious somewhere. I asked him to please stop talking. The fourth one burned while we argued.
plate seven
Save food for someone who is late.

Saved Toma's meal. Eight became nine, cold drawer at ten. Then they brought his boots in taped shut at the tops. Blue tape. Contamination or checked? I can never remember. Nobody explained. Went back to the kitchen and left the drawer open till it beeped. A wet footprint on the floor in front of it. Bare foot, leading under the tables. I'd just mopped. I don't like where this is going but the meal was still there.
inspection grade B
An inspector misses the point.

The inspector wanted hairnets. We had two, both filtering the tank water. I offered to shave my head. He wrote that down. Wanted the handwashing station next. I showed him the bucket. He wrote that down too. Passing the sleeping racks he noticed a child's drawing. Apparently there was no child on the manifest. The manifest also said fresh vegetables, which I pointed out. He stopped writing. Behind the rack someone sneezed. I wish I'd made up something better than vegetables. It made the whole thing sound less serious than it was.
Celebrate with limited materials.

We didn't know his birthday because the calendar reset during the jump. Made a cereal cake anyway. Used the red emergency lamp for a candle. He stared at it and said thirty four, not thirty five. Nobody had said an age. The cake started sagging round the battery compartment. I'd got the lamp from damaged stores. Reached for it. He caught my wrist hard.
wash cycle
An ordinary task after a difficult day.

I washed the same bowl three times. Each time I put it down I thought of the alarm and picked it up again. The water had gone grey. Somebody was singing in the next compartment, very badly, and I wanted to go in and tell them to stop but I also didn't want them to stop. It was the only noise that wasn't a machine. I turned the bowl over. There was a crack right through the bottom. I'd been washing a broken bowl for twenty minutes.
half past six
Someone delays leaving work.

The cleaner needed the keys but Colin was still in the office. He said he was waiting for an email. The cleaner said he could get emails at home. Colin said it was confidential. This was not true. He was waiting for the car park to empty because he had hit someone's car and he wanted to see whose it was without standing beside it. From the upstairs window he could only see the roof. It was blue. There were three blue cars and he had forgotten which bay. At six thirty the cleaner came upstairs with a mop and said the manager had called to ask who was still there. Colin said just me. She said I know that, what should I tell him. He did not have a good answer.
The display
A shop rearranges something familiar.

They moved the baby clothes where the shoes had been. The shelves were too deep. Anna said so but nobody changed them. A woman wanted a size they didn't have. Anna looked in the returns bag anyway. There was one shirt, with her own surname written on the label. It wasn't a common name. She checked it again.
five short
A small amount matters.
He was five pence short. I put five pence in. Then he wanted a different loaf which cost more. I didn't know if he expected me to pay that too. He just stood there. I stood there as well.
Training day
Teach someone a task you do automatically.

I told the new man to count the boxes before signing. He counted them and signed. Then I told him to open one and check the contents. He asked why I hadn't told him that before he signed. I said I thought it was obvious. It wasn't obvious. Inside the box there were twenty four empty packets with the seals intact. We opened another and that was the same. The driver had already gone. The new man wanted to phone the number on the delivery sheet but I knew it would be the office, and the office would ask why we'd signed. I put one packet in my pocket. It felt heavier once it was there. I took it out and it was still empty. There was something wrong with it but I couldn't explain what.
No order this week
A familiar customer stops coming.

Mrs Hall stopped buying her usual food on Wednesdays. After three weeks her son came in for beer and said she was fine. I wanted this to be a mystery but maybe she was fine. Maybe she was using a different shop. We had put the prices up. I don't think there's any reason for the narrator to go to her house. I keep trying to make him.
Saturday staff
An ordinary day feels different.

The manager came in wearing a suit on Saturday. He never worked Saturdays. He went into the back room and asked us to come in one at a time. I was third. While I waited I tidied the discount table even though it was already tidy. The first person came out and went straight to her locker. The second came out and started serving somebody. Both seemed normal. When it was my turn the manager asked me to shut the door. He had a list with my name on it. My name was spelled wrong. I pointed that out, which was probably not the first thing I should have said. He crossed it out and wrote it again, still wrong, and I sat down without correcting him.
